drafter.private_reasoning: Opposing counsel wants to limit Seller's indemnity to claims arising before Closing and exclude post-Closing regulatory matters, to protect their client's interests. However, our client has a pending regulatory probe (Pembrook), which is a significant undisclosed liability that would likely arise post-Closing. Therefore, we must keep the indemnity clause broad to cover both pre-Closing and post-Closing regulatory claims to protect our client from post-Closing exposure. We can propose a compromise to clarify the timing of claims but insist on including regulatory matters without limitation. This balances their interests while protecting our client against the undisclosed liability risk. We can add clarifying language that indemnity covers any claims related to circumstances existing as of Closing, including those discovered or arising post-Closing. We will draft our counterproposal accordingly.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We appreciate your proposal to tighten the indemnity clause; however, given the nature of certain contingencies existing as of Closing, including regulatory matters, we must ensure the Seller remains liable for all claims and losses arising from pre-Closing conditions, irrespective of whether such claims manifest post-Closing. Accordingly, our revised indemnity clause clarifies that the Seller indemnifies the Buyer against all losses arising from circumstances existing as of Closing, including any pending or future regulatory matters related thereto. We believe this approach fairly balances the protection of both parties' interests. Please review our proposed language below.
